question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x-2y-2z&=4 \\ -2x-y-4z&=-1 \\ 2x+y+6z&=7\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & -2 & -2 & 4 \\ -2 & -1 & -4 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 6 & 7\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ -2 & -1 & -4 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 6 & 7\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_2:=R_2+2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 2 & 1 & 6 & 7\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & -1 & 4 & 11\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3+R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 2 & 6\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=\frac{1}{2}R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 1 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & -5 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+y+z&=-2 \\ y-2z&=-5 \\ z&=3\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=3 \\ y&=-5-(-2)(3)=1 \\ x&=-2-(1)(1)-(1)(3)=-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle -6,1,3\rangle$.

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}-2x+4y-2z&=-4 \\ y&=3 \\ x&=10\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix $M$ of the system to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-2 & 4 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 10\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_1:=-\frac{1}{2}R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 1 & 0 & 0 & 10\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-R_1$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 2 & -1 & 8\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=R_3-2R_2$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -1 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

Using $R_3:=-1R_3$, we obtain

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -2\end{array}\right].
$$

The matrix is in row echelon form: each pivot lies to the right of the pivot above it, with zeros below each pivot.

The corresponding triangular system is

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x-2y+z&=2 \\ y&=3 \\ z&=-2\end{aligned}\right..
$$

Back substitution gives

$$
\begin{aligned}z&=-2 \\ y&=3-(0)(-2)=3 \\ x&=2-(-2)(3)-(1)(-2)=10.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $\langle 10,3,-2\rangle$.

\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & -1\end{array}\right].

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -2 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & -1\end{array}\right].
